land.text: Tuva, which became a Russian protectorate (Uryankhay Krai) in April 1914 and reaffirmed it after 1917

predecessors.note: Cliopatria has the Uryankhay Republic 1912-1913; the protectorate years 1914-1921 belong to russian-empire.

land.text: the Tuvan Autonomous Oblast within the Russian SFSR from 1 November 1944; Tuvan ASSR from 10 October 1961

successors.note: TP: accession decided 7 August, accepted 11 October, in effect 1 November 1944.

capitals.name: Khem-Beldyr (Kyzyl)
capitals.note: TP: 'changed the name of its capital from Khem-Beldyr to Kyzyl' in 1926; the coordinates are Kyzyl's, from the gazetteer (the page gives none).

correction.text: the territory of the Tannu Tuva People's Republic: modern Tuva less the strip Mongolia gave up in July 1932; the page names no component

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe, no Cliopatria row after 1913: infobox 170,500 km2 for 1944 against about 159,600 km2 for the Tuva region cells (ratio 0.94). The pre-1932 strip (Dus-Dag mountain among the 'territory from Mongolia') cannot be located from the pages, so the 1921-31 shape is the same region and slightly generous.

correction.text: Tuva after 'gained territory from Mongolia, including Dus-Dag mountain' in July 1932 (TP)

keyframe_review.note: New keyframe: the 1932 gain; Mongolia ratified the original 1932 agreement only in 1944 (TP). A 1940 border agreement was never ratified.

ledger.note: 1921: the Tannu Tuvan People's Republic declares independence. 'the Tannu Tuvan People's Republic ... declared independence' on 14 August 1921; its 1921 constitution said it 'acts under the auspices of Soviet Russia'. The area is the researcher's reading of Tuva (TU: a Russian protectorate since April 1914). Counterpart (reviewer, ia-03-x): the Bolsheviks 'had, by March 1921, seized all of Tuva' (TP), so the land comes from the Soviet state, not the Russian Empire (ended 1917).
1926: the country becomes simply the Tuvan People's Republic and the capital Khem-Beldyr is renamed Kyzyl. Mongolia and the USSR (1924, 1926) were its only formal recognisers.

region.text: territory from Mongolia including Dus-Dag mountain, inside Tuva

ledger.note: 1932: Tuva gains land from Mongolia. 'In July 1932 Tuva gained territory from Mongolia, including Dus-Dag mountain', in an agreement Mongolia signed under Soviet pressure. The extent is on no page; the region is the republic's own area.

1944: Tuva joins the Soviet Union. The TPRP Central Committee decided on 7 August 1944; 'The Presidium of the Supreme Soviet accepted' the accession on 11 October; it took effect on 1 November as the Tuvan Autonomous Oblast.

certainty.note: The frontier with Mongolia and China was undefined.
The Soviet-Tuvan border was defined in January 1923; the Mongolian line stays approximate until 1932.
The July 1932 agreement with Mongolia set the line (ratified by Mongolia only in 1944); the unratified 1940 agreement is not used.

sources.title: Tuvan People's Republic
sources.note: Proclaimed 14 August 1921, Kyzyl, Soviet and Mongolian recognition, border of January 1923, the July 1932 gain from Mongolia, annexation 1944, area 170,500 km2.

sources.title: Tannu Uriankhai
sources.note: The Russian protectorate of April 1914 that preceded the republic; annexed 1944.

notes: Written for batch ia-03-x from two pages (TP, TU; budget 1-2). Not on the pages: the Chinese and Mongol control of 1918-1921, Ungern, the entry of the Red Army, and the strip transferred in 1932 (only 'Dus-Dag mountain' is named). The republic was a Soviet client: TP gives the 1921 constitution's clause, the RSFSR agreement of summer 1925 ('did not consider Tannu-Tuva as its territory') and Soviet-Mongolian recognition in 1924 and 1926; no vassal pair is recorded because no page dates a protectorate. The rulers are not listed (Donduk Kuular PM in the 1920s, removed January 1929; Salchak Toka leader from 1932). The renderer may want the russian-empire and USSR dossiers to carry the client relation.
